title: Mechanical Aquarium Orrery
description: A steampunk mechanical aquarium where interlocking gears drive the orbital swimming paths of multiple BarramundiFish. The user controls gear rotation speeds, fish orbit radii, and animation easing curves through coupled sliders, with full undo/redo support. A conservation law ensures total mechanical energy (sum of gear angular momentum × fish orbital velocity) remains constant—speeding one gear automatically slows others.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements a Mechanical Aquarium Orrery. Load BarramundiFish.glb and gears.glb using GLTFLoader. Scene setup: dark blue-gray background (#1a2a3a), a PerspectiveCamera at (0,4,8) looking at origin, OrbitControls for viewing, ambient light (0.3 intensity) plus two directional lights (warm gold and cool blue) for dramatic steampunk lighting. Place the gears model at the center, scaled appropriately, and clone it to create 3 interlocking gear instances arranged in a triangular layout on the XZ plane. Clone the fish model 3 times, each fish orbiting one gear. Each fish swims in an elliptical orbit around its paired gear, with the fish tangentially oriented along its path and a subtle sinusoidal vertical bob. Implement a conservation system: define total energy E=constant. Each gear has angular velocity ω_i and each fish has orbital speed v_i, constrained so Σ(ω_i × v_i) = E. When the user changes one gear's speed via its slider, redistribute the others proportionally to conserve E. Build a UI panel with: 3 gear speed sliders (0.1–3.0), 3 orbit radius sliders (1.0–4.0), an easing dropdown (linear, easeInOut, elastic) affecting fish interpolation, and Undo/Redo buttons. Every slider or dropdown change pushes a snapshot (all parameter values) onto an undo stack (max 20). Undo restores the previous snapshot and pushes current to redo stack. Redo reverses this. Animate gears rotating around Y-axis at their respective ω_i. Fish orbit positions update each frame using elapsed time × v_i, applying the selected easing to radius transitions. Fish should face their movement direction using lookAt on the next path point. Ensure at least 10-14 meaningful interaction steps are possible through the coupled multi-input system.
